docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:694:docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/method42_v1_vs_v2_comparison.md:9:V1 numbers came from buggy NPZ where the SOM_MARKS regex `^\[\d+\]\s+\w+` extracted only 38 chars / 3 lines per task, dropping 71/72 marks. All Stage 4 cosine geometry was computed on near-empty text payloads where the only differentiator between flat-text modes (som / phantom_som / phantom_text) was prompt template. Modes still separated perfectly (AUROC 1.000) but the cosine-gap magnitudes were artifacts of prompt-template differences, not text-payload differences.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:741:docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/method42_v1_vs_v2_comparison.md:103:✅ §1 hero (drop-one CI strict-positive reddit + cls): unchanged
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:757:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section1_intro.md:7:Our first contribution is a controlled scientific evaluation of this phantom boundary. Across completed B0 VisualWebArena classifieds and reddit runs, we compare DOM, full SoM, Vision, and Phantom-SoM on the same task sets (**N=234 classifieds; N=210 reddit; same-task adjusted SR**) and use the P-text/P-prompt controls to test whether the effect collapses to one prompt trick or one text-format swap. Phantom-SoM is not the best single arm on every site, and we do not claim that it replaces full SoM. Its value is complementarity. Its task-success pool has low overlap with the established modes, with Jaccard similarity in the roughly **0.29-0.49** range against other arms, and its removal reduces the oracle. The principal hero metric is therefore the **drop-one oracle**, not the single-mode SR difference: Phantom-SoM contributes **3.33 percentage points** of incremental oracle value on reddit with a per-task-bootstrap 95% CI of **[+0.95, +6.19]** strictly above zero (P(Δ>0)=0.998, B=10000 task resamples), comparable to full SoM at +1.90pp [+0.48, +3.81], and **2.56 percentage points** on classifieds with CI [+0.85, +4.70] strict positive. Phantom-SoM consistently sits within the top routing-value arms despite using no image. The same bootstrap on the head-to-head reddit single-mode comparison (Phantom-SoM 13.81% vs full SoM 10.48%) gives a marginal CI [-0.95, +7.62] that crosses zero (P(diff>0)=0.914), which is exactly the "within 2σ" caveat above; we therefore frame the head-to-head SR contrast as competitive parity, and let the strictly-positive drop-one oracle carry the deployment-relevant claim. Crucially, the cost of obtaining this configuration is essentially the cost of the DOM baseline: the `[SOM_MARKS]` block is produced by a regex pass over the same accessibility-tree text the DOM agent already consumes (interactive elements come pre-numbered as `[N] role 'label'`), so a deployment that can run DOM can run Phantom-SoM by changing what it forwards to the model: no bounding-box pipeline, no marked image, no extra inference modality. We therefore preserve the empirical **4-fold drop-in property** as the paper's practical finding: cost approximately DOM, lower image-stage latency, usable routing signal, and positive drop-one oracle value.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:811:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section3_definition.md:29:Phantom-SoM uses the same SoM prompt family as full SoM and the same `[SOM_MARKS]` text, but removes the page screenshot passed to the model. In code, `p79/experiment/som.py::prepare_observation_for_mode` handles `mode in ("phantom_som", "phantom_dom", "phantom_text")` by calling `_build_som_result(...)`, then returning the generated `som_text` with `marked_image=None` (`phantom_dom` is the legacy mode value retained as alias for paper-grade run dirs; `phantom_text` is the current canonical name for P-text). The rendered screenshot path is retained for debugging; the model does not receive it.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:818:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section3_definition.md:52:Its observation is identical to Phantom-SoM: `[SOM_MARKS]` text only, no page screenshot. The only intended change is the system prompt. In both B0 (`p79/agents/proxy_api_agent.py`) and B1 (`p79/agents/qwen3vl_agent.py`), `_system_prompts["phantom_som"]` maps to the SoM prompt, while `_system_prompts["phantom_dom"]` (and the alias `_system_prompts["phantom_text"]`) maps to the DOM prompt. For `som`, `phantom_som`, `phantom_dom`, and `phantom_text`, the agent passes through the `[SOM_MARKS]...[/SOM_MARKS]` text directly.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:833:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section3_definition.md:86:When comparing arms, we use same-task subsets: a task contributes only when the relevant conditions have completed it. We report **adjusted SR**, which starts from raw evaluator success and removes `na_fp` for not-applicable tasks that appear correct without agent-initiated finish, and `eval_fp` for evaluator matches caused by ineffective or non-finished trajectories. Section 4 reports results under these conventions; Section 5 uses the same traces for mechanism analysis.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:834:docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/exp5_axis2_causal_patching.md:9:| Source | `phantom_som` (no image, flat `[SOM_MARKS]`, SoM prompt) | `som` (image, flat `[SOM_MARKS]`, SoM prompt) |
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:835:docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/exp5_axis2_causal_patching.md:10:| Target | `phantom_text` (no image, flat `[SOM_MARKS]`, DOM prompt) | `phantom_text` (same) |
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:837:docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/exp5_axis2_causal_patching.md:15:**Test logic**: Holding both `image` and `text-format` constant (off + flat) and patching source hidden states from `phantom_som` into a `phantom_text` run isolates whether the residual-stream prompt-family signature has *causal* effect on token continuation, not just *geometric* magnitude (which Exp 1 already showed is small at 0.011 cosine gap @ L23).
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:864:docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/exp5_axis2_causal_patching.md:101:- Patching displacement is a token-level metric; doesn't directly translate to SR / drop-one oracle. Behavioral consequence (which paper §1 hero is about) operates on top of this causal signal.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:2462:     7	VWA success labels are imperfect measurements of task completion, especially around `ua_match` GPT-judge drift, the `string_match` `fuzzy_threshold` misnomer, brittle `program_html` selectors, and `finish_wrong_state` episodes. The blast radius is measurement-side: these four evaluator-class threats can flip individual labels or inflate raw success, but they do not redefine the task universe or the mode definitions; full appendix prose is kept in Section 4.X.1--4.X.4 rather than duplicated here. We therefore report both raw and adjusted success and isolate `na_fp`, `eval_fp`, and `visual_fp` filters as sensitivity layers, including the audit-derived false-positive filters from Sections 78a and 95, following the constraint-table rule that evaluator artifacts should be disclosed rather than hidden \citep{lipton2018troubling,neurips2024checklist}. This affects Sections 3 and 4: adjusted SR is the headline metric, raw SR remains visible, and claims that survive the filter ladder are defensible as representation effects rather than judge artifacts.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:3743:    37	This matters because many cost reductions trade away information: smaller models, shorter context windows, lower image resolution, or fewer retrieved lines. Phantom-SoM instead tests whether a cheap re-arrangement of already available text can expose a different reasoning path. If it succeeds on tasks missed by DOM, the gain is not merely compression; it is complementarity. That is why Section 4 reports both single-mode success and drop-one oracle value rather than treating token savings alone as the contribution.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:3751:    45	The resulting gap is therefore a characterization gap, not a first-deployment gap. Published systems and benchmarks have not, to our knowledge, provided a controlled scientific evaluation of the phantom boundary: `[SOM_MARKS]` isolated from the screenshot, crossed with prompt family in a 2-by-2 control, compared through low-overlap success pools and drop-one oracle value, and checked against mechanistic controls including mid-layer L11-L17 evidence and random injection. This is also where the 4-fold drop-in property belongs. It is an empirical finding about a controlled configuration: zero image tokens, no new model, usable routing signal, and positive incremental oracle value. It is not a claim that text-only browser control or marked observations were first introduced here.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4271:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:58:Activation patching provides the causal test. For each task, the clean/source run and corrupt/target run use the same archived browser step and deterministic 50-token continuation. In the core SoM-to-Phantom-SoM setup, the source prompt is `som`: task instruction, SoM prompt family, flat `[SOM_MARKS]` text, and annotated screenshot. The target prompt is `phantom_som`: the same instruction, same prompt family, and same `[SOM_MARKS]` text, but no image. Source hidden states are cached by layer, injected into the final input-token position of the target on the first forward pass, and subsequent decoding proceeds normally through the model cache.

The bridge from patching displacement to behavioral SR remains open.

Phantom-SoM 的 single-mode superiority 不稳，但 drop-one oracle 是正的。Paper 自己写得正确：reddit head-to-head CI crosses zero，而 drop-one CI strict-positive（`section1_intro.md:7`）；evidence 给出 `phantom_som +3.33pp [0.95, 6.19], P(Δ>0)=0.998`（`hero_claim_bootstrap_ci.md:31-42`）。
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4402:   **Attack** — 这已经被你自己的 v2 audit 反证。`method42_v1_vs_v2_comparison.md:77-80` 明确说 `P-text/P-SoM ↔ Vision` 从 L36 shift 到 L04，breaks dichotomy；cls v2 JSON 也显示 `phantom_text_vs_vision` 和 `phantom_som_vs_vision` peak L04 (`method42_metrics_v2.json:2067-2101`)。  
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4407:   **Attack** — 当前只是 final-token replacement 对 50-token continuation 的 overlap metric，不是 task success, routing, or natural mediation。Exp 5 自己承认 “doesn't directly translate to SR / drop-one” and needs CIs (`exp5_axis2_causal_patching.md:97-101`)，而 paper table 还说 task-shuffled control in flight (`section5_mechanism.md:20`)。  
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4438:- Blocker 2: causal patching does not yet bridge to task behavior. Blocks “mechanism explains hero drop-one.”

docs/analysis/phantom_paper/B0_dom_shopping_diagnostic.md:133:B0 DOM shopping is not simply weaker or stronger than classifieds/reddit; it shifts the capability profile. Adjusted DOM SR is 13.55% on shopping, 14.10% on classifieds, and 8.10% on reddit. Shopping's raw DOM SR is the highest of the three (16.56%), but its adjusted SR drops by 3.0 points due to 14 `na_fp` cases. The failure mix is also different: shopping is dominated by `fail_no_progress` (37.4%) and `fail_finish_eval_mismatch` (28.4%), classifieds has more wrong-url failures (18.8% DOM), and reddit has more search-repeat/max-step behavior (13.8% DOM search-repeat).

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_methodology_audit_2026-05-12_v1_directive.md:878:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:57:Activation patching provides the causal test. For each task, the clean/source run and corrupt/target run use the same archived browser step and deterministic 50-token continuation. In the core SoM-to-Phantom-SoM setup, the source prompt is `som`: task instruction, SoM prompt family, flat `[SOM_MARKS]` text, and annotated screenshot. The target prompt is `phantom_som`: the same instruction, same prompt family, and same `[SOM_MARKS]` text, but no image. Source hidden states are cached by layer, injected into the final input-token position of the target on the first forward pass, and subsequent decoding proceeds normally through the model cache.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_methodology_audit_2026-05-12_v1_directive.md:902:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:130:This layered hierarchy partially resolves the Phantom-SoM hero puzzle without requiring a non-mechanistic explanation. Phantom-SoM occupies three distinct axis positions: **large image-axis separation from SoM** at L17 (0.0412 cosine gap, the largest single signal — note this is a *separation* from SoM, not a proximity; the no-image marks-text reshapes how image-axis divergence accumulates rather than recovering an image-like internal state), **small prompt-family separation from P-text** at L23 (0.011 signal, consistent across cls and reddit), and **medium text-format separation from P-prompt** at L23 (0.029 signal). P-text occupies only the text-format separation; P-prompt occupies only the prompt-family separation against P-SoM; DOM occupies none of the three. The drop-one hero status of Phantom-SoM in `fig_meta_forest.png` therefore corresponds to the only mode that simultaneously expresses all three axis positions. The connection from "three-axis positional uniqueness" to "drop-one task-success contribution" is currently associational, not yet causally bridged — the patching evidence shows residual-stream displacement on 50-token continuation, not direct displacement of task-level SR / drop-one oracle. Closing that behavioral causal bridge is open work.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_methodology_audit_2026-05-12_v1_directive.md:6665:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:130:This layered hierarchy partially resolves the Phantom-SoM hero puzzle without requiring a non-mechanistic explanation. Phantom-SoM occupies three distinct axis positions: **large image-axis separation from SoM** at L17 (0.0412 cosine gap, the largest single signal — note this is a *separation* from SoM, not a proximity; the no-image marks-text reshapes how image-axis divergence accumulates rather than recovering an image-like internal state), **small prompt-family separation from P-text** at L23 (0.011 signal, consistent across cls and reddit), and **medium text-format separation from P-prompt** at L23 (0.029 signal). P-text occupies only the text-format separation; P-prompt occupies only the prompt-family separation against P-SoM; DOM occupies none of the three. The drop-one hero status of Phantom-SoM in `fig_meta_forest.png` therefore corresponds to the only mode that simultaneously expresses all three axis positions. The connection from "three-axis positional uniqueness" to "drop-one task-success contribution" is currently associational, not yet causally bridged — the patching evidence shows residual-stream displacement on 50-token continuation, not direct displacement of task-level SR / drop-one oracle. Closing that behavioral causal bridge is open work.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_methodology_audit_2026-05-12_v1_directive.md:6816:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section4_empirical_findings.md:63:The overlap view supports the same conclusion. In the four-arm oracle, Phantom-SoM contributes a concrete reddit-only set of seven tasks (**7, 15, 36, 94, 157, 162, 167**) and a non-zero classifieds set as well. Two examples illustrate the kind of work this arm is doing. On reddit task 7, Phantom-SoM searched for the cake-recipe post and navigated directly to the OP recipe comment permalink. On reddit task 162, it searched within /f/wallstreetbets, scrolled hot posts, and returned the GIF URL for the retirement-account-versus-brokerage-account prompt. These are not proof of a universal mechanism by themselves, but they make the drop-one value concrete: the arm is adding recoverable successes, not only shifting aggregate percentages.

docs/analysis/phantom_paper/phantom_dom_vs_som_diagnostic.md:5:This audit compares fresh B0 P-text and Phantom-SoM runs on classifieds and reddit. The old "prompt only changes commitment confidence" theory is too narrow. On classifieds, P-text and Phantom-SoM have identical adjusted SR (34/234, 14.53%) but solve substantially different task sets: only 21 adjusted successes overlap, giving Jaccard 0.447. On reddit, the premise that the two adjusted SRs are equal is not supported by episode-level `adjusted_success`: P-text has 25/210 adjusted successes (11.90%), while Phantom-SoM has 29/210 (13.81%), with Jaccard 0.543. The best update is: the prompt family acts as a task-conditional decision prior over search terms, clicks, backtracking, and finish timing; commitment calibration is a real second-order subeffect, but not the only prompt knob.
docs/analysis/phantom_paper/phantom_dom_vs_som_diagnostic.md:7:Important data note: `condition_summary_v2.json` stores raw `success_rate`. For reddit P-text it reports raw 29/210 = 13.81%, but the episode summaries contain 4 raw-success false positives, so adjusted SR is 25/210 = 11.90%. All overlap and oracle-style claims below use episode-level `adjusted_success` unless a row is explicitly marked raw.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:101:- **Hero status confound**: "P-SoM (SoM-prompt + flat + no-image) vs P-text (DOM-prompt + flat + no-image) — drop-one difference could be ALL prompt — you haven't isolated"
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:210:    37	This matters because many cost reductions trade away information: smaller models, shorter context windows, lower image resolution, or fewer retrieved lines. Phantom-SoM instead tests whether a cheap re-arrangement of already available text can expose a different reasoning path. If it succeeds on tasks missed by DOM, the gain is not merely compression; it is complementarity. That is why Section 4 reports both single-mode success and drop-one oracle value rather than treating token savings alone as the contribution.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:218:    45	The resulting gap is therefore a characterization gap, not a first-deployment gap. Published systems and benchmarks have not, to our knowledge, provided a controlled scientific evaluation of the phantom boundary: `[SOM_MARKS]` isolated from the screenshot, crossed with prompt family in a 2-by-2 control, compared through low-overlap success pools and drop-one oracle value, and checked against mechanistic controls including mid-layer L11-L17 evidence and random injection. This is also where the 4-fold drop-in property belongs. It is an empirical finding about a controlled configuration: zero image tokens, no new model, usable routing signal, and positive incremental oracle value. It is not a claim that text-only browser control or marked observations were first introduced here.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:231:     7	Our first contribution is a controlled scientific evaluation of this phantom boundary. Across completed B0 VisualWebArena classifieds and reddit runs, we compare DOM, full SoM, Vision, and Phantom-SoM on the same task sets (**N=234 classifieds; N=210 reddit; same-task adjusted SR**) and use the P-text/P-prompt controls to test whether the effect collapses to one prompt trick or one text-format swap. Phantom-SoM is not the best single arm on every site, and we do not claim that it replaces full SoM. Its value is complementarity. Its task-success pool has low overlap with the established modes, with Jaccard similarity in the roughly **0.29-0.49** range against other arms, and its removal reduces the oracle. The principal hero metric is therefore the **drop-one oracle**, not the single-mode SR difference: Phantom-SoM contributes **3.33 percentage points** of incremental oracle value on reddit with a per-task-bootstrap 95% CI of **[+0.95, +6.19]** strictly above zero (P(Δ>0)=0.998, B=10000 task resamples), comparable to full SoM at +1.90pp [+0.48, +3.81], and **2.56 percentage points** on classifieds with CI [+0.85, +4.70] strict positive. Phantom-SoM consistently sits within the top routing-value arms despite using no image. The same bootstrap on the head-to-head reddit single-mode comparison (Phantom-SoM 13.81% vs full SoM 10.48%) gives a marginal CI [-0.95, +7.62] that crosses zero (P(diff>0)=0.914), which is exactly the "within 2σ" caveat above; we therefore frame the head-to-head SR contrast as competitive parity, and let the strictly-positive drop-one oracle carry the deployment-relevant claim. Crucially, the cost of obtaining this configuration is essentially the cost of the DOM baseline: the `[SOM_MARKS]` block is produced by a regex pass over the same accessibility-tree text the DOM agent already consumes (interactive elements come pre-numbered as `[N] role 'label'`), so a deployment that can run DOM can run Phantom-SoM by changing what it forwards to the model: no bounding-box pipeline, no marked image, no extra inference modality. We therefore preserve the empirical **4-fold drop-in property** as the paper's practical finding: cost approximately DOM, lower image-stage latency, usable routing signal, and positive drop-one oracle value.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:270:    29	Phantom-SoM uses the same SoM prompt family as full SoM and the same `[SOM_MARKS]` text, but removes the page screenshot passed to the model. In code, `p79/experiment/som.py::prepare_observation_for_mode` handles `mode in ("phantom_som", "phantom_dom", "phantom_text")` by calling `_build_som_result(...)`, then returning the generated `som_text` with `marked_image=None` (`phantom_dom` is the legacy mode value retained as alias for paper-grade run dirs; `phantom_text` is the current canonical name for P-text). The rendered screenshot path is retained for debugging; the model does not receive it.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:293:    52	Its observation is identical to Phantom-SoM: `[SOM_MARKS]` text only, no page screenshot. The only intended change is the system prompt. In both B0 (`p79/agents/proxy_api_agent.py`) and B1 (`p79/agents/qwen3vl_agent.py`), `_system_prompts["phantom_som"]` maps to the SoM prompt, while `_system_prompts["phantom_dom"]` (and the alias `_system_prompts["phantom_text"]`) maps to the DOM prompt. For `som`, `phantom_som`, `phantom_dom`, and `phantom_text`, the agent passes through the `[SOM_MARKS]...[/SOM_MARKS]` text directly.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:327:    86	When comparing arms, we use same-task subsets: a task contributes only when the relevant conditions have completed it. We report **adjusted SR**, which starts from raw evaluator success and removes `na_fp` for not-applicable tasks that appear correct without agent-initiated finish, and `eval_fp` for evaluator matches caused by ineffective or non-finished trajectories. Section 4 reports results under these conventions; Section 5 uses the same traces for mechanism analysis.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:336:     5	Throughout this section, we distinguish three measurement conventions. **Raw SR** is the evaluator success rate in `condition_summary_v2.json`. **Adjusted SR** subtracts confirmed false-positive terminal answers on not-applicable or evaluator-mismatch tasks. **Same-task adjusted SR** uses the same task set for all arms within a site. Unless otherwise noted, claims use same-task adjusted SR on completed B0 VisualWebArena classifieds and reddit runs. We also treat small cell-to-cell differences cautiously: under same-condition repeats, we observe roughly **+/-5% task-set variance**, so individual differences below about **2 pp** should be interpreted as noise-floor evidence rather than stable rankings.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:350:    19	The first three arms are the original Phase 1 representation baselines. Phantom-SoM is the new ablation arm. P-text is a prompt-family control: it receives the same marks-text-only observation as Phantom-SoM but uses the DOM prompt. We report all five modes for descriptive SR, cost, and latency. For the main routing-value claim, we keep the primary drop-one oracle on the four-arm comparison used throughout the paper: DOM, SoM, Vision, and Phantom-SoM.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:356:    25	The single-mode success rates show a site-modulated effect. On classifieds, full SoM remains the strongest individual representation. On reddit, Phantom-SoM is at least competitive with the strongest baselines, while using no image input. The table reports adjusted SR, because Figures 1, 2, 7, and 8 use episode-level `adjusted_success` for the paper comparisons. The latency column is p95 step latency from `condition_summary_v2.json`; cost is average total cost per task.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:383:    52	Single-mode SR can hide routing value. A representation may have modest average SR while still solving tasks that the other arms miss. We therefore compute a drop-one oracle: form the oracle union over the four primary arms, remove one arm, and measure how much oracle SR falls. This loss is the arm's incremental contribution to the routing pool.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:392:    61	The reddit oracle is the stronger routing signal. Phantom-SoM has the largest nominal drop-one loss in the fresh four-arm oracle (**3.33 pp; N=210**), while DOM and SoM each contribute **1.90 pp** and Vision contributes **1.43 pp**. Because these are small absolute task counts, we do not read the ordering as a precise rank claim. The important point is that Phantom-SoM is comparable to the top routing-value arms and is not subsumed by DOM, SoM, or Vision.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:394:    63	The overlap view supports the same conclusion. In the four-arm oracle, Phantom-SoM contributes a concrete reddit-only set of seven tasks (**7, 15, 36, 94, 157, 162, 167**) and a non-zero classifieds set as well. Two examples illustrate the kind of work this arm is doing. On reddit task 7, Phantom-SoM searched for the cake-recipe post and navigated directly to the OP recipe comment permalink. On reddit task 162, it searched within /f/wallstreetbets, scrolled hot posts, and returned the GIF URL for the retirement-account-versus-brokerage-account prompt. These are not proof of a universal mechanism by themselves, but they make the drop-one value concrete: the arm is adding recoverable successes, not only shifting aggregate percentages.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:523:    46	Activation patching provides the causal test. For each task, the clean/source run and corrupt/target run use the same archived browser step and deterministic 50-token continuation. In the core SoM-to-Phantom-SoM setup, the source prompt is `som`: task instruction, SoM prompt family, flat `[SOM_MARKS]` text, and annotated screenshot. The target prompt is `phantom_som`: the same instruction, same prompt family, and same `[SOM_MARKS]` text, but no image. Source hidden states are cached by layer, injected into the final input-token position of the target on the first forward pass, and subsequent decoding proceeds normally through the model cache.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:596:   119	This layered hierarchy resolves the Phantom-SoM hero puzzle without requiring a non-mechanistic explanation. Phantom-SoM uniquely combines three contributions: residual-stream proximity to SoM on the image axis at L17 (the largest single signal, with image-feature reduction "as if image were present"), separation from P-text on the prompt-family axis at L23 (a small 0.011 signal but consistent across cls and reddit), and separation from P-prompt on the text-format axis at L23 (a medium 0.029 signal). P-text occupies only the text-format separation; P-prompt occupies only the prompt-family separation against P-SoM; DOM occupies none of the three. The drop-one hero status of Phantom-SoM in `fig_meta_forest.png` therefore corresponds to the only mode that satisfies all three axis criteria.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:633:     7	VWA success labels are imperfect measurements of task completion, especially around `ua_match` GPT-judge drift, the `string_match` `fuzzy_threshold` misnomer, brittle `program_html` selectors, and `finish_wrong_state` episodes. The blast radius is measurement-side: these four evaluator-class threats can flip individual labels or inflate raw success, but they do not redefine the task universe or the mode definitions; full appendix prose is kept in Section 4.X.1--4.X.4 rather than duplicated here. We therefore report both raw and adjusted success and isolate `na_fp`, `eval_fp`, and `visual_fp` filters as sensitivity layers, including the audit-derived false-positive filters from Sections 78a and 95, following the constraint-table rule that evaluator artifacts should be disclosed rather than hidden \citep{lipton2018troubling,neurips2024checklist}. This affects Sections 3 and 4: adjusted SR is the headline metric, raw SR remains visible, and claims that survive the filter ladder are defensible as representation effects rather than judge artifacts.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:2443:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:119:This layered hierarchy resolves the Phantom-SoM hero puzzle without requiring a non-mechanistic explanation. Phantom-SoM uniquely combines three contributions: residual-stream proximity to SoM on the image axis at L17 (the largest single signal, with image-feature reduction "as if image were present"), separation from P-text on the prompt-family axis at L23 (a small 0.011 signal but consistent across cls and reddit), and separation from P-prompt on the text-format axis at L23 (a medium 0.029 signal). P-text occupies only the text-format separation; P-prompt occupies only the prompt-family separation against P-SoM; DOM occupies none of the three. The drop-one hero status of Phantom-SoM in `fig_meta_forest.png` therefore corresponds to the only mode that satisfies all three axis criteria.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:2721:docs/analysis/phantom_paper/phantom_dom_vs_som_diagnostic.md:5:This audit compares fresh B0 P-text and Phantom-SoM runs on classifieds and reddit. The old "prompt only changes commitment confidence" theory is too narrow. On classifieds, P-text and Phantom-SoM have identical adjusted SR (34/234, 14.53%) but solve substantially different task sets: only 21 adjusted successes overlap, giving Jaccard 0.447. On reddit, the premise that the two adjusted SRs are equal is not supported by episode-level `adjusted_success`: P-text has 25/210 adjusted successes (11.90%), while Phantom-SoM has 29/210 (13.81%), with Jaccard 0.543. The best update is: the prompt family acts as a task-conditional decision prior over search terms, clicks, backtracking, and finish timing; commitment calibration is a real second-order subeffect, but not the only prompt knob.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-12.md:2722:docs/analysis/phantom_paper/phantom_dom_vs_som_diagnostic.md:7:Important data note: `condition_summary_v2.json` stores raw `success_rate`. For reddit P-text it reports raw 29/210 = 13.81%, but the episode summaries contain 4 raw-success false positives, so adjusted SR is 25/210 = 11.90%. All overlap and oracle-style claims below use episode-level `adjusted_success` unless a row is explicitly marked raw.

docs/analysis/cross_sites/tier5_evaluator_audit.md:8:Tier 5 finds evaluator-side bias in all three audited surfaces. The largest already-known issue is the `ua_match` N/A accept bias: for `reference_answers.fuzzy_match == "N/A"`, `StringEvaluator` first exact-matches `N/A`, then falls back to an LLM reason-equivalence judge. The prompt tells GPT that the task is inherently unachievable before it sees the reported reason, which makes blank or generic failure reports too easy to rationalize as "same". Our `na_fp` filter covers the common no-finish case, but not active `finish` actions with blank/generic answers.
docs/analysis/cross_sites/tier5_evaluator_audit.md:44:2. Active-finish N/A gap. Our filter preserves N/A successes when `agent_finished=True` (`p79/experiment/analysis.py:76-79`). In a 20-row spot check from non-archived `episode_reason_rows.csv`, the false positives removed by adjusted success were all non-finish N/A cases, but an adjusted-true N/A example exists with `final_action_type=finish` and empty `final_answer` for reddit task 31. Static implication: if the model actively emits a finish action but leaves the answer blank or generic, post-hoc `na_fp` does not challenge the GPT judge.
docs/analysis/cross_sites/tier5_evaluator_audit.md:52:- Covered: `na_fp` removes raw successes on N/A tasks when the agent did not actively finish. See `compute_adjusted_success` lines `76-79`, and cross-representation mirror lines `438-450`.
docs/analysis/cross_sites/tier5_evaluator_audit.md:115:- Raw `string_match` successes: 228. Adjusted successes: 141. Removed: 87, all `na_fp`.

docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/exp5_axis2_causal_patching.md:15:**Test logic**: Holding both `image` and `text-format` constant (off + flat) and patching source hidden states from `phantom_som` into a `phantom_text` run isolates whether the residual-stream prompt-family signature has *causal* effect on token continuation, not just *geometric* magnitude (which Exp 1 already showed is small at 0.011 cosine gap @ L23).
docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/exp5_axis2_causal_patching.md:100:- "phantom_som" archive vs "som" archive — the codebase uses same hidden-state extraction infrastructure but `--source-mode phantom_som` extracts without image. The pilot_summary template label "(with image — clean)" is a hardcoded artifact, not a runtime check. Manual verification of the archive contents (hidden state norms) would close a soundness gap.
docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/exp5_axis2_causal_patching.md:101:- Patching displacement is a token-level metric; doesn't directly translate to SR / drop-one oracle. Behavioral consequence (which paper §1 hero is about) operates on top of this causal signal.

    98	def compute_adjusted_success_batch(ep_df, benchmark_site: str, benchmark: str = "visualwebarena"):
    99	    """Add adjusted_success + fp_reason columns to ep_df.
   100	
   101	    Requires columns: task_id, success.
   102	    Returns ep_df with new columns added in-place.
   103	
   104	    Fast-path (§97 audit Step 2): if ep_df already carries `adjusted_success`
   105	    AND `fp_reason` columns (runner-computed since §97), skip recomputation.
   106	    The runner is the single source of truth; this batch path is kept for
   107	    backward compatibility with episode summaries written before §97.
   108	    """
   109	    # F22 audit fix 2026-05-09: fast-path now validates fp_reason values
   110	    # against the locked set {'', 'na_fp', 'eval_fp'} (preregistration §4
   111	    # primary FP filter). If any row has an unknown fp_reason (e.g. legacy
   112	    # 'visual_fp', 'adjustment_error'), recompute from scratch instead of
   113	    # trusting runner output.
   114	    ALLOWED_FP_REASONS = {"", "na_fp", "eval_fp"}
   115	    if (
   116	        not ep_df.empty
   117	        and "adjusted_success" in ep_df.columns
   118	        and "fp_reason" in ep_df.columns
   119	        and ep_df["adjusted_success"].notna().all()
   120	    ):
   121	        observed_reasons = set(
   122	            (str(v) if v is not None else "") for v in ep_df["fp_reason"].fillna("")
   123	        )
   124	        unknown_reasons = observed_reasons - ALLOWED_FP_REASONS
   125	        if not unknown_reasons:
   126	            return ep_df
   127	        # Unknown fp_reason found — fall through and recompute.
   128	        import warnings as _warnings
   129	        _warnings.warn(
   130	            f"compute_adjusted_success_batch: dropping cached adjusted_success "
   131	            f"because fp_reason contains unknown values {sorted(unknown_reasons)}; "
   132	            "recomputing from raw fields. (F22 audit guard)",
   133	            stacklevel=2,
   134	        )
   135	
   136	    na_ids = _load_na_task_ids(benchmark_site, benchmark)
   137	
   138	    # F21 audit fix 2026-05-09: do not coerce missing `agent_finished` to
   139	    # True. `bool(NaN)` is True in Python which would bypass na_fp/eval_fp
   140	    # downstream. Use pd.notna check first; pass None when missing.
   141	    import pandas as _pd
   142	
   143	    def _safe_bool(value):
   144	        if value is None or _pd.isna(value):
   145	            return None
   146	        return bool(value)
   147	
   148	    adj_results = ep_df.apply(
   149	        lambda r: compute_adjusted_success(
   150	            int(r["task_id"]), benchmark_site,
   151	            bool(r["success"]),
   152	            na_task_ids=na_ids,
   153	            agent_finished=_safe_bool(r["agent_finished"]) if "agent_finished" in r.index else None,
   154	            eval_type=str(r["eval_type"]) if ("eval_type" in r.index and _pd.notna(r["eval_type"])) else None,
   155	            has_effective_action=_safe_bool(r["has_effective_action"]) if "has_effective_action" in r.index else None,
   156	        ),
   157	        axis=1,
   158	    )
   159	    ep_df["adjusted_success"] = [r[0] for r in adj_results]
   160	    ep_df["fp_reason"] = [r[1] for r in adj_results]
   161	    return ep_df

   164	def _compute_pareto_front(points: List[Dict[str, float]], maximize: str, minimize: str) -> List[int]:
   165	    """Return indices of Pareto-optimal points (maximize one axis, minimize another).
   166	
   167	    Sweep order: by `maximize` desc, then `minimize` asc. A point joins the
   168	    front only when its `minimize` is strictly less than the running best —
   169	    `<=` would let dominated points (same minimize, lower maximize) sneak in.
   170	    """
   171	    indexed = list(enumerate(points))
   172	    indexed.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1].get(maximize, 0.0), x[1].get(minimize, 0.0)))
   173	    pareto_indices: List[int] = []
   174	    best_min = float("inf")
   175	    for idx, pt in indexed:
   176	        val = pt.get(minimize, float("inf"))
   177	        if val < best_min:
   178	            pareto_indices.append(idx)
   179	            best_min = val
   180	    pareto_indices.sort(key=lambda i: points[i].get(minimize, 0.0))
   181	    return pareto_indices

    59	def detect_benchmark_noise(error_message: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[bool, Optional[str]]:

    62

    65	    # is caught earlier by runner as fatal (re-raised), never reaches here.
    66	    if any(k in msg for k in ("model-api", "execute-api")):

    68	    if any(k in msg for k in ("captcha", "anti-bot", "blocked", "forbidden", "access denied")):

    70	    if any(k in msg for k in ("geo-restricted", "not available in your region", "location")):

    74	    if any(k in msg for k in (

    76	        "page closed", "context closed", "frame was detached",
    77	    )):
    78	        return True, "playwright_error"
    79	    if any(k in msg for k in (
    80	        "econnrefused", "econnreset", "epipe", "connection reset",
    81	        "connection refused", "network error", "fetch failed",

    86	    if "start_url_content_error" in msg:

    95	def p95(values: List[float]) -> float:
    96	    if not values:
    97	        return 0.0
    98	    if len(values) == 1:
    99	        return float(values[0])
   100	    ordered = sorted(values)
   101	    k = 0.95 * (len(ordered) - 1)
   102	    f = int(k)
   103	    c = min(f + 1, len(ordered) - 1)
   104	    return float(ordered[f] + (k - f) * (ordered[c] - ordered[f]))

   111	def net_saving(cost_baseline_total: float, cost_routed_model: float, cost_router_overhead: float) -> float:
   112	    """
   113	    Net saving for routed condition.
   114	
   115	    Baseline is compared against routed total cost reconstructed from:
   116	    routed_total = routed_model + routed_router_overhead
   117	    """
   118	    return _net_saving(cost_baseline_total, cost_routed_model, cost_router_overhead)

   121	def net_saving_latency(
   122	    latency_baseline_ms: float,
   123	    latency_routed_ms: float,
   124	    router_overhead_ms: float = 0.0,
   125	) -> float:
   126	    """Net latency saving between baseline and routed conditions.
   127	
   128	    `latency_routed_ms` MUST be the *end-to-end* routed latency that already
   129	    includes the router decision overhead (which is recorded inside each step's
   130	    `latency_ms.total`). Therefore we DO NOT add `router_overhead_ms` again —
   131	    it would double-count.
   132	
   133	    `router_overhead_ms` is kept as a parameter for symmetry with the other
   134	    net_saving_* functions and for diagnostic reporting (callers can pass 0).
   135	
   136	    Semantics: saving = baseline - routed. Positive = routing is faster.
   137	    """
   138	    return float(latency_baseline_ms) - float(latency_routed_ms)

   152	def estimate_step_flops(
   153	    input_text_tokens: int,
   154	    input_image_tokens: int,
   155	    output_tokens: int,
   156	    model_profile: str = "qwen3vl_4b",
   157	) -> Dict[str, float]:
   158	    """Estimate FLOPs per step based on token counts and model architecture.
   159	
   160	    Uses the standard 2*N*d^2 approximation for transformer layers
   161	    (covering Q/K/V/O projections + FFN ≈ 4x multiplier per layer).
   162	    """
   163	    profiles = {
   164	        "qwen3vl_4b": {
   165	            "d_model": 2560,
   166	            "n_layers_llm": 36,
   167	            "vit_d_model": 1280,
   168	            "vit_layers": 32,
   169	        },
   170	    }
   171	    p = profiles[model_profile]
   172	    d, L = p["d_model"], p["n_layers_llm"]
   173	    vit_d, vit_L = p["vit_d_model"], p["vit_layers"]
   174	
   175	    # ViT encoder: 2 * tokens * d^2 * layers * 4 (attention + FFN)
   176	    vit_flops = 2.0 * input_image_tokens * (vit_d ** 2) * vit_L * 4
   177	
   178	    # LLM prefill: 2 * total_input * d^2 * layers * 4
   179	    total_input = input_text_tokens + input_image_tokens
   180	    llm_prefill_flops = 2.0 * total_input * (d ** 2) * L * 4
   181	
   182	    # LLM decode: 2 * output * d^2 * layers * 4
   183	    llm_decode_flops = 2.0 * output_tokens * (d ** 2) * L * 4
   184	
   185	    return {
   186	        "vit_encoder": vit_flops,
   187	        "llm_prefill": llm_prefill_flops,
   188	        "llm_decode": llm_decode_flops,
   189	        "total": vit_flops + llm_prefill_flops + llm_decode_flops,
   190	    }
   191

   193	def compute_wasted_cost(
   194	    step_records: List[Dict[str, Any]],
   195	    success: bool,
   196	    *,
   197	    adjusted_success: Optional[bool] = None,
   198	) -> Dict[str, float]:
   199	    """For failed episodes, all step cost is wasted; for successful ones, wasted is 0.
   200	
   201	    `adjusted_success` (optional, §95): when provided and False, the episode
   202	    is treated as wasted even if raw `success` is True (FP episodes that
   203	    coincidentally matched the evaluator without the agent finishing the task).
   204	    """
   205	    # Use adjusted_success when provided; otherwise fall back to raw.
   206	    is_real_success = adjusted_success if adjusted_success is not None else success
   207	    if is_real_success:
   208	        return {"wasted_cost_usd": 0.0, "wasted_energy_kwh": 0.0}
   209	    # Defensive: cost_usd / energy may be explicitly None on partial rows.
   210	    total_cost = sum(float((s.get("cost_usd") or {}).get("total", 0)) for s in step_records)
   211	    total_energy = sum(float((s.get("energy") or {}).get("kwh", 0) or 0) for s in step_records)
   212	    return {"wasted_cost_usd": total_cost, "wasted_energy_kwh": total_energy}

   236	        "page_unchanged_cost_usd": page_unchanged_cost,
   237	        "wasted_cost_usd": total_cost if not success else 0.0,

   100	def bootstrap_diff_ci(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray, B: int = 10000, seed: int = 42):

   107	        diffs[k] = 100 * (a[idx].mean() - b[idx].mean())

   111	        "ci_hi": float(np.quantile(diffs, 0.975)),
   112	        "p_gt_0": float((diffs > 0).mean()),
   113	        "p_gt_1pp": float((diffs > 1.0).mean()),
   114	        "median": float(np.median(diffs)),
   115	    }

   136	        "p_gt_0": float((drops > 0).mean()),

   136	def cohen_h(p1: float, p2: float) -> float:
   137	    """Cohen's h effect size between two proportions p1, p2 ∈ [0, 1].
   138	
   139	    h = 2 * (arcsin(√p1) - arcsin(√p2))
   140	
   141	    Interpretation: |h|<0.2 small, 0.2-0.5 medium, 0.5-0.8 large, >0.8 huge.
   142	    Sign indicates direction (p1 > p2 → h > 0).
   143	    """
   144	    p1 = max(0.0, min(1.0, p1))
   145	    p2 = max(0.0, min(1.0, p2))
   146	    return 2 * (math.asin(math.sqrt(p1)) - math.asin(math.sqrt(p2)))

   150	    a = abs(h)
   151	    if a < 0.2:
   152	        return "small"
   153	    if a < 0.5:
   154	        return "medium"
   155	    if a < 0.8:
   156	        return "large"
   157	    return "huge"

   160	def wilcoxon_signed_rank(in_a: np.ndarray, in_b: np.ndarray) -> tuple[Optional[float], Optional[float]]:
   161	    """Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired binary task outcomes (a vs b).
   162	
   163	    For binary outcomes diff ∈ {-1, 0, +1}; scipy drops zero diffs. When set b
   164	    ⊇ set a (e.g. 5-mode oracle ⊇ 3-mode oracle), all non-zero diffs are
   165	    positive (b solves task that a doesn't) → test reduces to one-sided
   166	    binomial (sign test). Returns (statistic, p_two_sided) or (None, None) if
   167	    scipy unavailable / undefined.
   168	    """
   169	    if not HAS_SCIPY:
   170	        return None, None
   171	    diffs = in_b.astype(int) - in_a.astype(int)
   172	    nonzero = diffs[diffs != 0]
   173	    if len(nonzero) == 0:
   174	        return None, 1.0  # no difference, p = 1
   175	    try:
   176	        with warnings.catch_warnings():
   177	            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
   178	            stat, p = sp_stats.wilcoxon(diffs, zero_method="wilcox", alternative="two-sided")
   179	        return float(stat), float(p)
   180	    except Exception:
   181	        return None, None
   182	
   183	
   184	def mcnemar_exact_one_sided(in_a: np.ndarray, in_b: np.ndarray) -> Optional[float]:
   185	    """McNemar exact one-sided p-value: H1 = b > a (b adds tasks a misses).
   186	
   187	    For monotonic case (b ⊇ a), discordant b-only count = sum(b - a > 0),
   188	    a-only count = 0. Exact binomial: p = 0.5^(b_only).
   189	    """
   190	    if not HAS_SCIPY:
   191	        return None
   192	    a = in_a.astype(int); b = in_b.astype(int)
   193	    a_only = int(((a > b)).sum())
   194	    b_only = int(((b > a)).sum())
   195	    n_disc = a_only + b_only
   196	    if n_disc == 0:
   197	        return 1.0
   198	    # one-sided: H1 = b > a
   199	    return float(sp_stats.binom.cdf(a_only, n_disc, 0.5))
   200	
   201	
   202	def bootstrap_unique_count_ci(in_a: np.ndarray, in_b: np.ndarray,
   203	                              B: int = 1000, seed: int = 42, ci: float = 0.95
   204	                              ) -> tuple[int, float, float]:
   205	    """Bootstrap CI on |a ∖ b| count: tasks where a solves but b doesn't.
   206	
   207	    H3 structural claim test: arm a contributes tasks NOT solved by arm b.
   208	    If lower CI bound > 0, "a has unique non-overlap with b" sig at 1-ci level.
   209	
   210	    Used per-cell for:
   211	      P-text ∖ P-SoM unique count (axis 1 structural evidence)
   212	      P-prompt ∖ P-SoM unique count (axis 2 structural evidence)
   213	    """
   214	    n = len(in_a)
   215	    if n == 0 or len(in_b) != n:
   216	        return 0, 0.0, 0.0
   217	    a = in_a.astype(bool)
   218	    b = in_b.astype(bool)
   219	    observed = int((a & ~b).sum())
   220	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   221	    counts = np.empty(B)
   222	    for r in range(B):
   223	        idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)
   224	        counts[r] = int((a[idx] & ~b[idx]).sum())
   225	    alpha = (1 - ci) / 2
   226	    return observed, float(np.quantile(counts, alpha)), float(np.quantile(counts, 1 - alpha))
   227

   229	def bootstrap_tost_equivalence_p(in_a: np.ndarray, in_b: np.ndarray,

   231	                                  ) -> Optional[float]:

   235	    H1: |true lift| < δ           (effect equivalent to zero within margin)

   237	    Two one-sided tests:

   239	                              p_lower = P(boot_lift <= -δ); small p_lower
   240	                              ⇒ evidence rejects "effect <= -δ"
   241	      H0_upper:  lift >= +δ  → reject if bootstrap dist mostly below +δ
   242	                              p_upper = P(boot_lift >= +δ); small p_upper
   243	                              ⇒ evidence rejects "effect >= +δ"
   244	
   245	    TOST p = max(p_lower, p_upper).
   246	    **If max(p_lower, p_upper) < α, equivalence is ACCEPTED** — both
   247	    one-sided tests reject, so the effect is bounded inside (-δ, +δ).
   248	
   249	    F03 audit fix 2026-05-09: δ default = 1.0pp (was 0.5). Matches
   250	    `preregistration.md §4` lock "TOST equivalence margin δ = 1.0pp".
   251	
   252	    F04 audit fix 2026-05-09: renamed from `bootstrap_tost_p`; clarified
   253	    docstring (previous wording said "equivalence rejected when max < α"
   254	    which inverts the conclusion). Strong positive lift gives p_upper≈1
   255	    correctly (effect is outside +δ equivalence margin), so equivalence
   256	    is correctly NOT accepted.
   257	
   258	    For the **nonzero / one-sided directional** test (the phantom-lift
   259	    hypothesis "lift > 0"), use `bootstrap_one_sided_nonzero_p()` below.
   260	    """

   309	        return float(np.mean(lifts <= 0.0))
   310	    elif alternative == "less":
   311	        return float(np.mean(lifts >= 0.0))
   312	    else:
   313	        raise ValueError(f"alternative must be 'greater' or 'less', got {alternative}")

   315	
   316	def bonferroni_adjust(pvals: list) -> list:
   317	    """Bonferroni: p_adj = min(1, m * p_raw); None entries pass-through."""
   318	    m = sum(1 for p in pvals if p is not None)
   319	    if m == 0:
   320	        return list(pvals)
   321	    return [min(1.0, m * p) if p is not None else None for p in pvals]
   322	
   323	
   324	def holm_bonferroni_adjust(pvals: list) -> list:
   325	    """Holm-Bonferroni step-down (Holm 1979): less conservative than Bonferroni
   326	    while still controlling family-wise error rate at α.
   327	
   328	    Sort non-None p-values ascending; the k-th smallest gets multiplied by
   329	    (m - k + 1) where m = number of non-None tests; running max enforces
   330	    monotonicity.
   331	    """
   332	    indexed = [(i, p) for i, p in enumerate(pvals) if p is not None]
   333	    indexed.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
   334	    m = len(indexed)
   335	    out: list = [None] * len(pvals)
   336	    prev = 0.0
   337	    for k, (i, p) in enumerate(indexed):
   338	        adj = min(1.0, max(prev, p * (m - k)))
   339	        out[i] = adj
   340	        prev = adj
   341	    return out
   342	
   343	
   344	def bh_fdr_adjust(pvals: list) -> list:
   345	    """Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjusted q-values (BH 1995).
   346	
   347	    Less conservative than FWER methods; controls expected proportion of false
   348	    discoveries among rejections rather than family-wise error rate.
   349	    """
   350	    indexed = [(i, p) for i, p in enumerate(pvals) if p is not None]
   351	    indexed.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
   352	    m = len(indexed)
   353	    out: list = [None] * len(pvals)
   354	    prev = 1.0
   355	    for k in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
   356	        i, p = indexed[k]
   357	        rank = k + 1
   358	        adj = min(prev, p * m / rank)
   359	        out[i] = min(1.0, adj)
   360	        prev = out[i]
   361	    return out

    65	def _f(x):
    66	    if x is None or x == "" or x == "None":
    67	        return None
    68	    return float(x)

    70	
    71	def derslong_laird_meta(thetas: list, ses: list) -> Optional[dict]:
    72	    """DerSimonian-Laird random-effect meta-analysis.
    73	
    74	    Args:
    75	        thetas: per-cell point estimates (pp scale)
    76	        ses: per-cell SEs (matched to thetas)
    77	
    78	    Returns dict with k / theta_fe / se_fe / theta_re / se_re / ci_lo / ci_hi /
    79	    Q / df / p_Q / tau2 / I2, or None if no data.
    80	    """
    81	    paired = [(t, s) for t, s in zip(thetas, ses) if t is not None and s is not None and s > 0]
    82	    if len(paired) == 0:
    83	        return None
    84	    thetas_arr = np.array([t for t, _ in paired])
    85	    ses_arr = np.array([s for _, s in paired])
    86	    k = len(paired)
    87	
    88	    # Fixed-effect (inverse-variance weighted)
    89	    var_i = ses_arr ** 2
    90	    w_i = 1.0 / var_i
    91	    theta_fe = float(np.sum(w_i * thetas_arr) / np.sum(w_i))
    92	    se_fe = float(math.sqrt(1.0 / np.sum(w_i)))
    93	
    94	    # Cochran's Q (heterogeneity test statistic)
    95	    Q = float(np.sum(w_i * (thetas_arr - theta_fe) ** 2))
    96	    df = k - 1
    97	    if HAS_SCIPY and df > 0:
    98	        p_Q = float(1 - sp_stats.chi2.cdf(Q, df))
    99	    else:
   100	        p_Q = None
   101	
   102	    # τ² (between-study variance, DL estimator)
   103	    if df > 0:
   104	        sum_w = float(np.sum(w_i))
   105	        sum_w2 = float(np.sum(w_i ** 2))
   106	        C = sum_w - sum_w2 / sum_w
   107	        tau2 = max(0.0, (Q - df) / C) if C > 0 else 0.0
   108	    else:
   109	        tau2 = 0.0
   110	
   111	    # I² (% variation due to heterogeneity, Higgins & Thompson 2002)
   112	    if Q > 0 and df > 0:
   113	        I2 = max(0.0, (Q - df) / Q) * 100.0
   114	    else:
   115	        I2 = 0.0
   116	
   117	    # Random-effect estimate (using w*_i = 1 / (var_i + tau2))
   118	    var_star = var_i + tau2
   119	    w_star = 1.0 / var_star
   120	    theta_re = float(np.sum(w_star * thetas_arr) / np.sum(w_star))
   121	    se_re = float(math.sqrt(1.0 / np.sum(w_star)))
   122	    ci_lo = theta_re - 1.96 * se_re
   123	    ci_hi = theta_re + 1.96 * se_re
   124	
   125	    # RE vs 0 z-test (single-side: pooled effect > 0)
   126	    z = theta_re / se_re if se_re > 0 else None
   127	    if HAS_SCIPY and z is not None:
   128	        p_re = float(1 - sp_stats.norm.cdf(z))
   129	    else:
   130	        p_re = None
   131	
   132	    return {
   133	        "k": k,
   134	        "theta_fe": theta_fe,
   135	        "se_fe": se_fe,
   136	        "theta_re": theta_re,
   137	        "se_re": se_re,
   138	        "ci_lo": ci_lo,
   139	        "ci_hi": ci_hi,
   140	        "z_re": z,
   141	        "p_re_one_sided": p_re,
   142	        "Q": Q,
   143	        "df": df,
   144	        "p_Q": p_Q,
   145	        "tau2": tau2,
   146	        "I2": I2,
   147	    }
   148	
   149	
   150	def i_squared_label(I2: float) -> str:
   151	    if I2 < 25:
   152	        return "low"
   153	    if I2 < 50:
   154	        return "moderate"
   155	    if I2 < 75:
   156	        return "substantial"
   157	    return "considerable"
   158

   160	# F08 audit fix 2026-05-09: B8 preregistration lock requires N_common >= 10
   161	# per cell for inclusion in random-effects meta. Cells below floor are
   162	# excluded with reason logged. See `preregistration.md §4` row "Heterogeneity
   163	# (random-effects, Q, I², τ²) pre-spec".
   164	MIN_N_COMMON_FOR_META = 10
   165	
   166	
   167	def load_per_cell_data(arm_code: str) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
   168	    """Per-cell point + SE for a given arm, with B8 N>=10 floor enforced.
   169	
   170	    Returns (included, excluded) cell-row dicts. SE_i derived from bootstrap
   171	    CI: SE = (CI_hi - CI_lo) / (2 * 1.96).
   172	    """
   173	    if not CSV_IN.exists():
   174	        raise SystemExit(f"missing {CSV_IN}; run aggregate_phantom_lift.py first")
   175	    included, excluded = [], []
   176	    with CSV_IN.open() as f:
   177	        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
   178	        for r in reader:
   179	            theta = _f(r.get(f"lift_{arm_code}_pp"))
   180	            ci_lo = _f(r.get(f"lift_{arm_code}_ci95_lo_pp"))
   181	            ci_hi = _f(r.get(f"lift_{arm_code}_ci95_hi_pp"))
   182	            n_common = _f(r.get("n_common"))
   183	            cell_label = f"{r.get('baseline','?')} {r.get('site','?')}"
   184	            if theta is None or ci_lo is None or ci_hi is None:
   185	                continue
   186	            se = (ci_hi - ci_lo) / (2 * 1.96)
   187	            if se <= 0:
   188	                continue
   189	            row = {
   190	                "baseline": r["baseline"],
   191	                "site": r["site"],
   192	                "n_common": int(n_common) if n_common is not None else None,
   193	                "theta": theta,
   194	                "se": se,
   195	                "ci_lo": ci_lo,
   196	                "ci_hi": ci_hi,
   197	            }
   198	            if n_common is not None and n_common < MIN_N_COMMON_FOR_META:
   199	                row["exclude_reason"] = f"N_common={int(n_common)} < {MIN_N_COMMON_FOR_META} (B8 lock)"
   200	                excluded.append(row)
   201	                continue
   202	            included.append(row)
   203	    return included, excluded
   204	
   205	
   206	def main() -> int:
   207	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   208	    ap.add_argument("--output", default=str(DEFAULT_OUT))
   209	    args = ap.parse_args()
   210	
   211	    out = Path(args.output)
   212	    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   213	
   214	    meta_rows = []
   215	    arm_per_cell: dict = {}
   216	    arm_excluded: dict = {}  # F08: track B8 N>=10 floor exclusions
   217	    for code, label, family in ARMS:
   218	        cells, excluded = load_per_cell_data(code)
   219	        arm_per_cell[code] = cells
   220	        arm_excluded[code] = excluded
   221	        if excluded:
   222	            for ex in excluded:
   223	                print(
   224	                    f"  [B8 floor] arm={code} excluded "
   225	                    f"{ex['baseline']} {ex['site']}: {ex['exclude_reason']}"
   226	                )
   227	        if not cells:
   228	            continue
   229	        meta = derslong_laird_meta(
   230	            [c["theta"] for c in cells],

   232	        )
   233	        if meta is None:
   234	            continue
   235	        meta_rows.append({
   236	            "arm_code": code,
   237	            "arm_label": label,
   238	            "family": family,
   239	            "k_cells": meta["k"],
   240	            "cells": "; ".join(f"{c['baseline']} {c['site']}" for c in cells),
   241	            "excluded_b8": "; ".join(

   243	                for c in excluded
   244	            ) or "none",
   245	            **{k: round(v, 6) if isinstance(v, float) else v
   246	               for k, v in meta.items() if k != "k"},
   247	        })
   248	
   249	    # CSV
   250	    with out.open("w", newline="") as f:
   251	        if meta_rows:
   252	            w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(meta_rows[0].keys()))
   253	            w.writeheader()
   254	            w.writerows(meta_rows)
   255	    print(f"wrote {out} ({len(meta_rows)} arms)")
   256	
   257	    # Markdown
   258	    md = out.with_suffix(".md")
   259	    n_arms = len(meta_rows)
   260	    n_primary = sum(1 for r in meta_rows if r["family"] == "PRIMARY")

# Hero-claim bootstrap CI (W1 defuse)

Per-seed bootstrap 95% percentile CI on paired adjusted-SR diffs and drop-one oracle. B=10000, seed=42. Tasks resampled with replacement at task level.

**Defuse target**: /stress W1 attack — paper §1 hero claim 'P-SoM 13.81% > SoM 10.48% reddit' is statistically marginal under author's own 2σ hedge.

## reddit (N=210 same-task)

**Per-mode adjusted SR (%)**:

- dom: 9.52%
- som: 10.48%

     2	from __future__ import annotations
     3	
     4	import json
     5	import logging
     6	from pathlib import Path
     7	from typing import Any, Dict, List
     8	
     9	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    10	
    11	
    12	def dedup_restart_lines(file_lines: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    13	    """Keep only the last run when a JSONL has restart artifacts.
    14	
    15	    The runner appends to JSONL (mode='a'), so if the watchdog/queue
    16	    restarts a task, earlier runs' steps remain in the file.  We detect
    17	    restarts by step_idx resetting to 0 and keep lines from the last run
    18	    (matching the authoritative summary_v2.json which is overwritten).
    19	    """
    20	    if not file_lines:
    21	        return file_lines
    22	    last_run_start = 0
    23	    for i, rec in enumerate(file_lines):
    24	        if i > 0 and rec.get("step_idx", -1) == 0:
    25	            last_run_start = i
    26	    if last_run_start > 0:
    27	        logger.debug(
    28	            "Dedup: discarded %d lines from earlier run(s)", last_run_start
    29	        )
    30	    return file_lines[last_run_start:]
    31	
    32	
    33	def read_jsonl_dedup(path: Path) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    34	    """Read a single JSONL file, deduplicating restart artifacts."""
    35	    file_lines: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    36	    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    37	        for line_num, line in enumerate(f, 1):
    38	            line = line.strip()
    39	            if not line:
    40	                continue
    41	            try:
    42	                file_lines.append(json.loads(line))
    43	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
    44	                logger.warning("Dropped corrupt JSONL line %d in %s: %.100s", line_num, path, line)
    45	                continue
    46	    return dedup_restart_lines(file_lines)

    20	    if name in ("m4", "m4_two_stage", "m4_two_stage_generation_grounding"):

    25	def _load_best_condition_from_phase1(path: Path) -> Optional[Tuple[bool, str, str]]:
    26	    """
    27	    Returns tuple(som_on, observation_mode, condition_id) from phase1 run summary if available.
    28	    """
    29	    if not path.exists():
    30	        return None
    31	
    32	    # Accept either run root or direct run_summary.json path
    33	    summary_path = path
    34	    if path.is_dir():
    35	        summary_path = path / "run_summary_v2.json"
    36	    if not summary_path.exists():
    37	        return None
    38	
    39	    with open(summary_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    40	        payload = json.load(f)
    41	
    42	    condition_metrics = payload.get("condition_metrics", [])
    43	    if not condition_metrics:
    44	        return None
    45	
    46	    # Highest success, then lower cost, then lower latency.
    47	    ranked = sorted(
    48	        condition_metrics,
    49	        key=lambda x: (
    50	            float(x.get("success_rate", 0.0)),
    51	            -float(x.get("avg_total_cost_usd", 0.0)),
    52	            -float(x.get("p95_step_latency_ms", 0.0)),
    53	        ),
    54	        reverse=True,
    55	    )
    56	    top = ranked[0]
    57	    obs_mode = str(top.get("observation_mode", "som"))
    58	    som_on = obs_mode == "som"
    59	    return som_on, obs_mode, str(top.get("condition_id", "phase1_best"))

    25	    marks: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    31	        label = re.sub(r"\[(\d+)\]", "", line).strip()

   178	    if mode == "phantom_prompt":

   192	def _build_som_result(
   193	    obs: Any,
   194	    obs_text: str,
   195	    artifact_dir: Path,
   196	    step_idx: int,
   197	    include_full_axtree: bool = False,
   198	) -> SomResult:
   199	    """Core SOM logic: build SOM_MARKS index + marked image.
   200	
   201	    Args:
   202	        include_full_axtree: If True, appends the full AXTree after SOM_MARKS
   203	            (legacy behavior). If False (new SOM mode), only SOM_MARKS is returned.

   213	        # Fall back to the raw (unmarked) screenshot so the model can still use vision.
   214	        return SomResult(
   215	            som_text="[SOM_MARKS]\n[/SOM_MARKS]",
   216	            marked_image_path=None,

   218	            degraded_som=True,

   223	    # '[OPTIONS: currently selected="x"] ...' or '[DROPDOWN OPTIONS] ...').
   224	    # _inject_select_options / _inject_css_dropdown_options already wrote these
   225	    # into obs_text (the full AXTree), but _extract_text_marks strips them because
   226	    # they have no [N] element id.  Re-scan obs_text to recover them.
   227	    _options_map: Dict[int, str] = {}
   228	    _obs_lines = (obs_text or "").splitlines()
   229	    for _i, _line in enumerate(_obs_lines):
   230	        _m = re.search(r"\[(\d+)\]", _line)
   231	        if not _m:
   232	            continue
   233	        _eid = int(_m.group(1))
   234	        for _j in range(_i + 1, min(_i + 3, len(_obs_lines))):
   235	            _stripped = _obs_lines[_j].strip()
   236	            if _stripped.startswith("[OPTIONS") or _stripped.startswith("[DROPDOWN OPTIONS"):
   237	                _options_map[_eid] = _stripped
   238	                break
   239	            if re.search(r"\[(\d+)\]", _obs_lines[_j]):
   240	                break  # next element reached
   241	
   242	    mark_lines = []
   243	    for _mark in text_marks:
   244	        _entry = f"[id={_mark['id']}] {_mark['label']}"
   245	        if _mark["id"] in _options_map:
   246	            _entry += f"\n    {_options_map[_mark['id']]}"
   247	        mark_lines.append(_entry)
   248	
   249	    som_header = "\n".join(["[SOM_MARKS]"] + mark_lines + ["[/SOM_MARKS]"])
   250	    som_text = f"{som_header}\n\n{obs_text}" if include_full_axtree else som_header
   251	
   252	    bbox_map: Dict[int, List[float]] = {}
   253	
   254	    # Prefer VWA's obs_nodes_info (populated from CDP via observation_metadata).
   255	    # Each entry: str(element_id) -> {"union_bound": [x, y, width, height], ...}
   256	    # Convert [x, y, w, h] → [x1, y1, x2, y2] for _normalize_bbox.
   257	    obs_nodes_info = getattr(obs, "obs_nodes_info", None)
   258	    if obs_nodes_info:
   259	        for node_id_str, node_info in obs_nodes_info.items():
   260	            try:
   261	                eid = int(node_id_str)
   262	                ub = node_info.get("union_bound") if isinstance(node_info, dict) else None
   263	                if ub and len(ub) == 4 and all(v is not None for v in ub):
   264	                    x, y, w, h = (float(v) for v in ub)
   265	                    if w > 0 and h > 0:
   266	                        bbox_map[eid] = [x, y, x + w, y + h]
   267	            except (ValueError, TypeError):
   268	                continue
   269	    else:
   270	        # Fallback: attempt to collect bboxes from raw obs dict (legacy path).
   271	        raw = getattr(obs, "raw", None)
   272	        _collect_bbox_map(raw, bbox_map)
   273	
   274	    image = getattr(obs, "image", None)
   275	    marked_image_path: Optional[str] = None
   276	    marked_image: Optional[Any] = None
   277	
   278	    if image is not None and bbox_map:
   279	        try:
   280	            drawn = image.copy()
   281	            draw = ImageDraw.Draw(drawn)
   282	            width, height = drawn.size
   283	            font = _get_font(size=14)
   284	            for mark in text_marks:
   285	                bbox = bbox_map.get(mark["id"])
   286	                if not bbox:
   287	                    continue
   288	                x1, y1, x2, y2 = _normalize_bbox(bbox, width, height)
   289	                draw.rectangle([x1, y1, x2, y2], outline="#00BCD4", width=2)
   290	                _draw_label(draw, x1, y1, str(mark["id"]), font)
   291	
   292	            marked_image = drawn  # PIL Image passed to the model
   293	
   294	            som_dir = artifact_dir / "som"
   295	            som_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   296	            marked_image_path = str(som_dir / f"step_{step_idx:03d}_som.png")
   297	            drawn.save(marked_image_path)
   298	        except Exception:
   299	            logger.warning("SOM image rendering failed; degrading to unmarked screenshot", exc_info=True)
   300	            marked_image_path = None
   301	            marked_image = None
   302	
   303	    # degraded_som=True here means marks were extracted but image rendering failed.
   304	    # Zero-mark complete degradation is handled in the early return above.
   305	    degraded = marked_image is None
   306	    return SomResult(
   307	        som_text=som_text,
   308	        marked_image_path=marked_image_path,
   309	        marked_image=marked_image,
   310	        degraded_som=degraded,
   311	        mark_count=len(text_marks),
   312	    )
   313	
   314	
   315	def apply_som(
   316	    obs: Any,
   317	    som_on: bool,
   318	    artifact_dir: Path,
   319	    step_idx: int,
   320	) -> SomResult:
   321	    """Backward-compatible function. Prefer prepare_observation_for_mode for new code."""
   322	    obs_text = getattr(obs, "text", "") or ""
   323	    if not som_on:
   324	        return SomResult(som_text=obs_text, marked_image_path=None, marked_image=None, degraded_som=False, mark_count=0)
   325	    return _build_som_result(obs, obs_text, artifact_dir, step_idx, include_full_axtree=True)

   273	def _collect_condition_summaries(run_dir: Path) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   274	    rows: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   275	    seen_conds: set = set()
   276	    # 1. Completed conditions (have condition_summary_v2.json)
   277	    for summary_path in run_dir.glob("*/condition_summary_v2.json"):
   278	        with open(summary_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   279	            data = json.load(f)
   280	            rows.append(data)
   281	            seen_conds.add(summary_path.parent.name)
   282	
   283	    # 2. In-progress conditions (have condition_meta.json but no summary)
   284	    for meta_path in run_dir.glob("*/condition_meta.json"):
   285	        cond_dir = meta_path.parent
   286	        if cond_dir.name in seen_conds:
   287	            continue
   288	        if cond_dir.name.startswith("_"):
   289	            continue
   290	        # Load episode summaries for this condition
   291	        ep_summaries = []
   292	        for ep_path in cond_dir.glob("episodes/*_summary_v2.json"):
   293	            with open(ep_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   294	                ep_summaries.append(json.load(f))
   295	        if not ep_summaries:
   296	            continue
   297	        synth = _synthesize_condition_summary(cond_dir, ep_summaries)
   298	        if synth:
   299	            logger.info(
   300	                "Synthesized condition summary for %s (%d episodes, in-progress)",
   301	                cond_dir.name, len(ep_summaries),
   302	            )
   303	            rows.append(synth)
   304	
   305	    return rows

   448	            .agg(
   449	                episodes=("task_id", "count"),
   450	                episodes_with_failed=("checklist_failed", lambda s: int((s.fillna(0) > 0).sum())),
   451	                avg_completion_rate=("checklist_completion_rate", "mean"),

   453	            .fillna({"avg_completion_rate": 0.0})
   454	        )

   456	    if summary.empty:

   561	def _analyze_condition(
   562	    cond_id: str,
   563	    cond_dir: Path,
   564	    ep_rows: List[Dict[str, Any]],
   565	    step_rows: List[Dict[str, Any]],
   566	    phase: str,
   567	    run_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
   568	) -> None:
   569	    """Generate analysis for a single condition into analysis/<cond_id>/."""
   570	    try:
   571	        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # type: ignore
   572	        import pandas as pd  # type: ignore
   573	    except Exception:
   574	        return
   575	
   576	    out_dir = cond_dir
   577	    plots_dir = out_dir / "plots"
   578	    tables_dir = out_dir / "tables"
   579	    for d in (out_dir, plots_dir, tables_dir):
   580	        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   581	    # Remove stale plots/tables from previous runs so no stale files linger
   582	    for _f in plots_dir.glob("*.png"):
   583	        _f.unlink(missing_ok=True)
   584	    for _f in tables_dir.glob("*.csv"):
   585	        _f.unlink(missing_ok=True)
   586	
   587	    ep_df = pd.DataFrame(ep_rows)
   588	    step_df = pd.DataFrame(step_rows)
   589	
   590	    if not ep_df.empty:
   591	        ep_df.to_csv(tables_dir / "episode_metrics.csv", index=False)
   592	    if not step_df.empty:
   593	        step_df.to_csv(tables_dir / "step_metrics.csv", index=False)
   594	
   595	    # Noise report
   596	    if not ep_df.empty:
   597	        if "benchmark_noise" in ep_df.columns:
   598	            noise_df = ep_df[ep_df["benchmark_noise"] == True]  # noqa: E712
   599	        else:
   600	            noise_df = pd.DataFrame()
   601	        if not noise_df.empty:
   602	            noise_counts = noise_df.groupby("benchmark_noise_category").size().reset_index(name="count")
   603	            noise_counts.to_csv(tables_dir / "benchmark_noise_report.csv", index=False)
   604	
   605	    if ep_df.empty:
   606	        return
   607	
   608	    # --- Cumulative success rate curve ---
   609	    if "success" in ep_df.columns and "task_id" in ep_df.columns:
   610	        sr_df = ep_df[["task_id", "success"]].copy()
   611	        sr_df["success"] = pd.to_numeric(sr_df["success"], errors="coerce").fillna(0)
   612	        sr_df = sr_df.sort_values("task_id")
   613	        sr_df["cumulative_success_rate"] = sr_df["success"].expanding().mean()
   614	        sr_df.to_csv(tables_dir / "cumulative_success_rate.csv", index=False)
   615	        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
   616	        ax.plot(sr_df["task_id"], sr_df["cumulative_success_rate"])
   617	        ax.set_xlabel("Task ID")
   618	        ax.set_ylabel("Cumulative Success Rate")
   619	        ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
   620	        ax.set_title(f"Success Rate (adjusted) — {cond_id}")

   869	def _compute_statistical_tests(

   871	    ep_df,

   875	    """Compute bootstrap CIs, McNemar's test, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests."""

   878	        import pandas as pd  # type: ignore
